name: seed-bank-v3
prompt:
A seed bank tracks sample jars with a shelf ledger and a shipping manifest. Staff assign a permanent accession code when a jar arrives. A manifest number is assigned only if part of the sample is later shipped to another laboratory. Jar maple arrived first and received accession 501. Jar pine arrived next and received accession 502. The bank kept both jars sealed in the same climate-controlled room. On a later afternoon the staff prepared a shipment from pine and printed manifest 88. The following morning they prepared a shipment from maple and printed manifest 89. A visiting researcher saw the lower manifest number on pine and assumed pine had entered the seed bank before maple. The intake ledger, however, is signed at each arrival and lists maple before pine. The researcher also checked that accession codes were not recycled and that neither jar had been returned and readmitted. The shipping clerk explained that manifest numbers track outbound packages, not intake order, and that packages can be prepared in a different sequence from accession. The bank asks for a short clarification that preserves both facts: intake order and outbound paperwork order. State which jar arrived first and which jar was shipped first, naming the record that supports each claim.
